correctness.rationale: For all n>=7, a perfect matching cut is equivalent to a 0/1 coloring with exactly one opposite-color neighbor at every vertex. Outer colors uniquely determine inner colors; the 9-bit local test gives a bijection to closed walks in an explicitly defined 256-state digraph. All 512 potential arcs are exhausted; three exact rounds delete vertices absent from any closed walk and leave precisely two loops, one directed 4-cycle and two directed 5-cycles. This yields 2+4[4|n]+10[5|n] oriented colorings and the stated half-count of cuts. The 0,n/5,n crossing-spoke stratification follows by reading each orbit. A standalone C++17 checker reproduces the 90 arcs, state-core counts 42/20/16, exact 16 arcs, periodic closed walks to n=100, and brute-force original-edge colorings on 11,182,080 assignments for 7<=n<=12. Finitely checked orders are corroborative; the finite-state bijection and exhaustive 512-case certificate prove all n.

value.rationale: Cubic graph perfect matching cuts encode separations into two cycle-unions and are nontrivial to recognize in general. For the canonical GP(n,3) family this theorem completely enumerates and classifies every such separation, identifies sharp divisibility criteria for the additional cuts, and distinguishes three exact crossing-spoke strata. The new primitive period four coexists with period five, unlike the sole nonconstant period in the adjacent jump-two case; this is a structural resonance, not a numerical one-off. There is no claim of a general-k classification.
